haiku-low.q1: Only after the message commit succeeds, the Gateway sends the sender an ack containing msg_id and seq.
haiku-low.q2: Sender gets an error, no outbox row exists, and nobody receives anything. The retry must carry the same msg_id.
haiku-low.q3: After 30 seconds without a heartbeat, its Presence entry expires and the user counts as offline.
haiku-low.q4: It is treated as offline for that message: an Offline Inbox entry is written and a push is sent. A late ack deletes the entry.
haiku-low.q5: The failure is ignored and never retried. The Inbox entry remains, so the message arrives at the next sync.
haiku-low.q6: In seq order within each conversation. The client drops duplicates by msg_id and acks all received messages.
haiku-low.q7: The outbox row is written in the same transaction as the message. After a restart, the relay publishes unpublished rows, so fan-out still happens.
haiku-low.q8: The Presence Registry, a key-value store of user to gateway id. Its 30 s TTL expiry removes the entry when heartbeats stop.
haiku-low.q9: The Fan-out Worker makes an internal call to the gateway, which sends the message to the client. The client's ack returns as the call's reply.
haiku-low.q10: The per-user Offline Inbox. The Fan-out Worker writes it for offline recipients before the push. Client acks or 30-day expiry remove entries.
haiku-low.q11: The user's Offline Inbox, read after presence is registered, then the matching messages from the Message Store.
haiku-low.q12: The event is not committed, so the worker reprocesses it from the start. Recipients may get duplicates, which clients drop by msg_id.

sonnet.q1: Only after the message and outbox row are committed in the Message Store. The ack carries msg_id and seq (it does not wait for any recipient).
sonnet.q2: The sender gets an error; no outbox row exists and nobody receives anything. The retry must carry the same msg_id, so no second copy is created.
sonnet.q3: When no heartbeat arrives for 30 s, the Presence entry's TTL expires and the user counts as offline (heartbeats are sent every 10 s).
sonnet.q4: The recipient is treated as offline for that message: an Offline Inbox entry is written and a push is sent once. If the client acks late, its Gateway deletes the Inbox entry (the push may already have gone out).
sonnet.q5: It is ignored and never retried; it doesn't affect the Inbox or Message Store. The Inbox entry remains, so the message arrives at the next sync.
sonnet.q6: In seq order within each conversation. The client drops messages it already has by msg_id, and acks all of them.
sonnet.q7: The outbox: the message and outbox row are written in one transaction, so both are saved. The Relay later publishes unpublished rows to the Event Bus, so fan-out still happens after a crash.
sonnet.q8: In the Presence Registry, a key-value store of user to gateway id. Entries have a 30 s TTL refreshed by heartbeats, so the entry expires on its own when heartbeats stop.
sonnet.q9: The Fan-out Worker looks up the user's gateway in the Presence Registry and makes an internal call to that Gateway, which sends the message to the client. The client's ack, returned as the call's reply (waiting at most 5 s), confirms arrival.
sonnet.q10: In the per-user Offline Inbox (a list of conversation, seq, msg_id). It is written by the Fan-out Worker when a recipient is offline (idempotent per user and msg_id). Entries are removed when a Gateway receives the client's ack (deleting the entry for that msg_id), or by expiry after 30 days.
sonnet.q11: The Gateway first registers presence, then reads the user's Offline Inbox, which is the complete list of what to send. For each conversation it reads those messages from the Message Store and sends them in seq order.
sonnet.q12: The event is not committed, so it is processed again from the start. Some recipients may get duplicates, which clients drop by msg_id.
